text: Debugging is an essential skill for any programmer. When a program does not work as expected, the first step is identifying bugs by reproducing the error and understanding what causes it. Good debugging tools, such as breakpoints and step-by-step execution, help you examine your code closely. However, tools alone are not enough; you also need a systematic approach. This means forming a clear idea about the problem, testing one change at a time, and checking the results carefully. Logging is another useful strategy, because well-placed log messages record what your program is doing and make it easier to find where things go wrong.
